summary: No stack satisfies all hard constraints at once; the critical warnings name what blocks it and what to relax.

warnings.message: air-gapped deployment cannot run on AWS; the cloud preference is ignored and an on-premise host is used.
Every hosting option is excluded: air-gapped deployment allows only on-premise hosting; cloud_preference is aws and this runs on onprem.

If you allow any cloud provider instead of aws, a stack becomes possible: React Native (Expo) with Node.js + NestJS and PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted) on Self-managed Linux servers (on-premise) (core layers about $0-$8 per month).

If you use managed cloud services instead of air-gapped, a stack becomes possible: React Native (Expo) with Supabase (BaaS) and Supabase Postgres on AWS Amplify Hosting (core layers about $28-$100 per month).

assumptions: No extra inputs supplied; neutral defaults are used (learning appetite medium, lock-in tolerance medium, budget strictness firm, no hiring plan, no mobile preference).

pipeline: filter each layer by hard constraints
